channel.title: Stargazing Start
channel.description: What to look for in the night sky and how to find it.

item.title: How to Find the North Star (Polaris) Using the Big Dipper
item.description: A step-by-step way to find Polaris from the Big Dipper's pointer stars, why it marks true north, and how its height above the horizon reveals latitude.

item.title: Planning a Meteor Shower Night, What NASA Says
item.description: NASA's own numbers on how many meteors you can actually expect to see, why the often-quoted rate is misleading, and how to plan a realistic viewing night.

item.title: Reading Moon Phases for Better Stargazing Nights
item.description: A guide to what each moon phase means and why a dark sky matters for stargazing, based on NASA's official Moon Phases guidance.

item.title: Using Binoculars for Stargazing
item.description: Why binoculars are often recommended as a first stargazing tool over a telescope, based on official NASA skywatching guidance.

item.title: What You Can See With the Naked Eye Tonight
item.description: A guide to planets, stars, meteors, and other sights visible without equipment, based on official NASA and IAU skywatching resources.
